title: Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2024)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s consolidated finance and legal operating procedures for: annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement & purchase order (PO) workflows, contract lifecycle and legal review process, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering teams that execute purchases, negotiate agreements, or are responsible for subscription and usage-based billing.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood entities and product lines unless a specific country or customer agreement overrides these standards.
- Covers: annual budget cycle, quarterly reforecasts, capital vs expense guidelines, vendor procurement thresholds, contract review SLAs, standard contract clauses, revenue recognition for subscription and usage billings, invoicing cadence, and credit/refund treatment.

Owners and escalation:
- Document owner: Finance (owner_team) – Finance & Legal Ops (primary contact: Aisha Patel).
- Legal owner: Head of Legal (reviewer: Marcus Lee).
- Operational escalations: Finance lead -> Head of Finance -> CFO.
- Contract escalation (exceptions or bespoke clauses): Legal -> General Counsel.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
Overview:
- Annual budget is prepared on a fiscal-year basis with a rolling 12-month forecast maintained monthly. The budgeting process aligns to product roadmaps, hiring plans, infrastructure commitments (including Dedicated capacity and Private deployment investments), and go-to-market targets.

Timeline (annual):
1. Planning kickoff: mid-Oct (lead: Finance planning team)
2. Department submissions: Nov 1 - Dec 1
3. Cross-functional review & scenario analysis: Dec 1 - Dec 20
4. Executive review and finalization: Jan 1 - Jan 15
5. Board submission: Jan 20

Forecast cadence:
- Rolling forecast updated monthly with actuals through month-end. Re-forecast triggers: variance > 10% vs plan for a functional area or material contract change (> $250k ARR impact).

Inputs & assumptions:
- Headcount plan (by role and band) with hire timing
- Infrastructure and cloud commitments (expected Dedicated fleet spend, reserved instances)
- Model licensing and third-party model costs (quantization/license tiers)
- GTM spend (marketing, partnerships, sales commissions)
- ARR and usage growth scenarios (base / stretch / downside)

Budget controls & approvals:
- Department-level budgets (OPEX) require manager + director approval for line items <$50k; VP approval for $50k–$250k; CFO approval for >$250k. Capital requests follow capex evaluation form and require Finance + Head of Eng/Product sign-off and CFO approval for >$100k.

Reporting & tools:
- Primary tools: NetSuite (GL & reporting), Adaptive Planning (budgeting & forecasting), internal BI dashboards (Looker/Grafana for usage & cost metrics). Weekly exec dashboard highlights burn, ARR, cash runway, and major contract commitments.

2) Procurement & Purchase Order (PO) Procedures
Objective:
- Ensure control, cost-effectiveness, vendor compliance, and audit readiness for all purchases.

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Procurement team involvement | Docs required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <$5,000 | Dept Manager | Optional | Quote or invoice |
| $5,000 - $50,000 | Director + Procurement review | Procurement engaged for vendor selection | 2 competitive quotes or vendor justification |
| $50,000 - $250,000 | VP + Procurement + Finance | Procurement lead manages RFP if applicable | Approved SOW / vendor terms, risk assessment |
| >$250,000 | CFO + Legal + Procurement | Executive procurement process; Board notification if strategic | Contract, SOW, security & compliance sign-off |

Preferred vendors and catalogs:
- Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list with pre-negotiated terms (payment net 30/45, volume discounts, SLAs). For cloud/GPU capacity purchases, engage Infra Procurement early to evaluate committed vs on-demand pricing.

PO issuance and invoice matching:
1. Requestor submits purchase request in procurement system (ProcureFlow).
2. Procurement validates vendor, obtains quotes, and generates PO.
3. PO must be referenced on vendor invoices.
4. Finance performs 3-way match (PO, receipt of goods/service, invoice) before payment. Exceptions require Procurement + Finance sign-off.

Emergency/one-off purchases:
- For urgent operational needs (incidents impacting customer SLAs), Director-level approval can expedite PO issuance; Procurement must file retroactive documentation within 5 business days.

3) Contracts & Legal Process
Contract lifecycle overview:
1. Request & intake: Requestor completes contract intake form in ContractFlow.
2. Initial review: Legal triage for contract type (MSA, SOW, NDA, Channel Reseller, Partner Agreement).
3. Risk assessment: Identify data residency, KMS/HSM, liability caps, indemnity, IP assignments, export controls, and audit rights.
4. Negotiation: Legal to lead, with Finance providing commercial term guidance (price, billing cadence, revenue recognition implications).
5. Signature & execution: Use DocuSign with authorized signatory list maintained by Legal.
6. Contract entry: Store signed contract in the Contract Repository (Clause/DocStore).
7. Post-signature operations: Legal defines renewal notifications, obligation tracking, and SLA monitoring.

Standard clauses & redlines (summary):
- Limitation of liability: default cap is the greater of $500k or 12 months of fees; any exceptions require GC approval.
- Indemnity: Mutual indemnities for IP; customer indemnity for their data and third-party content.
- Data protection: Include SCCs or equivalent and specify data residency where required by customer. KMS/HSM requirement flagged for Private deployments.
- Security & audits: Right to audit clause limited to scope and frequency; SOC2 evidence and self-attestation accepted for standard customers.
- Termination for convenience: Default 30-day notice for vendor contracts; customer commercial contracts follow negotiated terms.

SLAs for Legal review:
- Standard NDAs and low-risk MSAs: 3 business days target.
- Customer MSAs with custom terms or complex data residency/KMS: 7–15 business days.
- Complex enterprise contracts (PSCAs, Government or regulated customers): 20+ business days; require Legal + Security + Compliance review.

Templates & guardrails:
- Legal publishes approved templates for: NDA, MSA (hosted + private variants), SOW, Reseller Agreement, Data Processing Agreement (DPA). Use templates to reduce review time. Any deviation must be highlighted in intake form.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles:
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 / IFRS 15 framework: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied.

Revenue types & recognition rules:
- Hosted API usage (pay-as-you-go): Recognize revenue as services are delivered (pro rata by consumption/date of service). Invoiced monthly in arrears; revenue recognized in the same period as service delivery.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) contracts: If fees are for reserving capacity (standby) with a committed monthly fee plus usage overage, split into capacity (recognized ratably over the committed period) and usage (recognized upon delivery).
- Private deployment (license + support): Perpetual license fees recognized when control transfers (rare); support and maintenance recognized ratably over the service period. For term licenses, recognize ratably over the license term.
- One-time professional services (integration, migration): Recognize over time if services create/modify an asset controlled by customer or if progress methods (milestones/time & materials) are applied; otherwise recognize at completion.

Billing cadence & invoicing:
- Standard customers: Monthly invoicing in arrears for usage, with net 30 payment terms unless otherwise contracted.
- Prepaid or committed ARRs: Recognize over the contracted term; invoice schedule per contract (monthly/quarterly/annual).
- Late payments: Interest at contractual rate (typically 1.5% monthly) and collections escalations after 30 days.

Deferred revenue & accounting treatment:
- Cash collected in advance is recorded to deferred revenue liability and released to revenue as performance obligations are satisfied.
- Significant implementation fees tied to future obligations are deferred and amortized over the term.

Credits, refunds & disputes:
- Credits for service disruption: Apply per SLA terms and customer agreement; Finance will issue credit memos and adjust deferred revenue if credit impacts recognized revenue.
- Billing disputes: Customer must submit dispute within 60 days of invoice. During the dispute period, disputed amounts may be offset or placed on hold pending resolution; resolution within 30 days is target.

Revenue controls & reconciliations:
- Monthly revenue close checklist: usage invoice reconciliation -> AR aging -> booking to GL -> deferred revenue roll-forward -> revenue recognized vs forecast.
- Reconciliations are documented and retained for audit (SOX / external audit) for at least 7 years.

5) Controls, Audit Evidence & Compliance
- Segregation of duties: Requestors, approvers, procurement, and payment processing are distinct roles; any conflicts require documented mitigations.
- Record retention: Contracts, POs, invoices, vendor due diligence, and security attestations retained per retention policy (7 years standard).
- Audit readiness: Maintain evidence bundles for material contracts and significant revenue streams (quarterly sample for review).
- SOX controls: Key controls documented in Control Atlas with control owners and evidence locations.

Appendices
A. Approval matrix (quick reference):
- Operational purchases <$5k: Manager approval
- Non-standard software/vendor engagements $5k–$50k: Director + Procurement
- Strategic vendor contracts >$250k: CFO + Legal + Procurement

B. Contract intake checklist (required at intake):
- Business owner & cost center
- Contract type and term
- Estimated financial impact (ARR, one-time fees)
- Data residency/KMS/HSM requirements
- Security evidence (SOC2, ISO certs)
- Renewal & termination clauses summary
